detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds RL support for **Step-5-Preview** (FP8 block-quantized MoE with sparse
DSA attention) on the FSDP2 engine. It covers GRPO with LoRA against a vLLM
rollout, rollout routing replay (R3), and adapter-only weight sync.

verl has no Step5 model, so the PR adds a verl-native text model and an example
recipe, plus the generic changes the run needed. 21 files; each commit can be
reviewed on its own:

| # | Commit | Files | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `[utils] fix: honor tokenizer.json when AutoTokenizer rebuilds the pre-tokenizer` | 1 | all models, only when the loaded tokenizer deletes whitespace that its `tokenizer.json` keeps |
| 2 | `[vllm] fix: treat untagged vLLM source builds as the newest API` | 6 | untagged vLLM builds (`0.1.devN`); the TCP-store path for every build |
| 3 | `[rollout, vllm] perf: stage LoRA buckets in one host block; optionally drop the adapter host copy` | 4 | LoRA sync to vLLM |
| 4 | `[fsdp] feat: support R3 router replay` | 4 | FSDP engine, off by default; LoRA reference routing in every engine |
| 5 | `[fsdp, model] feat: Step-5-Preview text model for FSDP2 LoRA RL` | 6 new + engine hooks | `model_type == "step5"` only |

**Dependency on vLLM.** Upstream vLLM does not serve Step5 yet. The rollout
needs a vLLM build with the Step5 model, LoRA serving on its fused attention
and sparse-indexer projections, and pageable host backups for level-1 sleep
(pinned backups made host memory grow on every sleep/wake cycle until OOM).
Those vLLM changes are being upstreamed separately. Until then this PR is a
draft; the verl side does not depend on any vLLM internals beyond the
existing LoRA/weight-sync paths.

**Overlap with open PRs. Please reconcile before merging.**

- #8193 addresses the same tokenizer failure as commit 1. Commit 1 acts only on
  the observed failure (whitespace deleted on a round trip, kept by the file),
  and refuses to load rather than swap when special tokens, added tokens, the
  vocabulary size, the chat template or the special tokens around plain text
  would change.
- #8194 is the same feature as commit 4. Here the FSDP engine turns R3 on
  while it builds the model, so VeOmni (which builds its own model and has its
  own replay hook) needs no change.

### Test

The PR carries no tests, to keep it reviewable. The checks written for it ran
against the final branch head in a Step5 vLLM image (transformers 5.17, an
untagged vLLM source build), with asserts enabled:

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Tokenizer: real Step-5-Preview tokenizer (swapped, encodes like `tokenizer.json`, same specials); configured `add_prefix_space`, stored truncation, `use_fast=False`, unresolvable ids left alone; refusal propagates through `hf_processor` | 22/22 |
| Version parsing and gates; a one-rank stateless process group built on the installed vLLM | 18/18 |
| R3 packing, alignment and refusals | 10 passed |
| LoRA bucket staging and the vLLM weight-update path | 27 passed, 5 skipped (shared-memory variants) |
| Step5 model pieces, checkpoint naming and sharded reads, LoRA attach and per-expert export, replay, grouped gathers (2 GPUs), startup refusals | 99 passed |

I can add any of them to the PR if reviewers want them in tree.

On this base (`f724e7f2`): ruff check/format pass on every changed file; the
generated trainer configs match `scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh` output.

**Training run.** The example recipe ran from scratch on 4 nodes x 4 GB300 for
194 steps (stopped there on purpose), as one run with two restarts from
LoRA-only checkpoints. It ran the code this PR was cut from: the same model,
LoRA math and sync logic. The review fixes since then add startup refusals and
guards (listed under Known gaps and Rollback) and do not change the numerics
of that configuration.

AIME-2024 during training (4096-token responses, as in the recipe):

| Step | 0 | 40 | 80 | 120 | 160 | 190 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean@8 | 0.375 | 0.375 | 0.500 | 0.575 | 0.571 | 0.658 |
| answers finished within 4096 tokens | 0.400 | | | | | 0.750 |

Most of that gain is answers finishing within the budget. To separate it, the
step-0 and step-190 checkpoints were re-evaluated with a 16384-token budget
(8 samples per problem; maj@8 and best@8 are verl's bootstrap estimates):

| AIME-2024, 16384 tokens | step 0 | step 190 |
|---|---|---|
| mean@8 | 0.804 | 0.829 |
| maj@8 | 0.832 | 0.911 |
| best@8 | 0.930 | 0.963 |
| answers finished | 0.829 | 0.963 |
| accuracy of finished answers | 0.970 | 0.861 |
| median answer length (characters) | 18,732 | 7,803 |

With room to finish, single-sample accuracy moves little (+0.025). The trained
model answers in less than half the length and finishes almost always; majority
voting gains 0.08. Accuracy on finished answers drops because the step-0 model
finishes mostly the problems it solves. Training responses show the same
trend: 41% truncated in steps 1–20, 18% in steps 181–194.

Over steps 1–194, trainer-vs-rollout agreement stayed stable:

- per-token mean abs logprob diff: 0.020–0.023 (20-step means);
- KL: about 0.001;
- rejected sequences: under 1% on average, at most 2.7% on one step;
- entropy: 0.74 → 0.57 (20-step means), smoothly;
- grad norm: mostly 0.004–0.013, with isolated spikes at steps 44 and 184.

These are aggregate run metrics; they do not show that each operation matches
the serving kernels (see the numerics item under Known gaps).

### API and Usage Example

```bash
# Needs a vLLM build that serves Step5 (see "Dependency on vLLM").
# ckpt_dir must be on storage shared by all nodes.
bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_step5_preview_dapo_lora_fsdp.sh
```

- Model: `stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview` (FP8). Data: DAPO-Math-17K for training,
  AIME-2024 for validation.
- 4 nodes x 4 GPUs, two TP8 vLLM engines; LoRA r32/α64, lr 1e-5 constant;
  R3; sequence-level geometric rejection (`seq_mean_k1`, 0.995–1.005), no IS
  weights; 4096-token responses.
- The recipe passes its environment to the Ray workers through
  `ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.env_vars`; a plain `export` does not reach
  workers of a pre-started cluster.
- Extra packages beyond verl's: `peft==0.21.2`, `accelerate==1.15.0`.
- Optional, for repeatable LoRA outputs: point `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` at a
  LoRA shrink config with `split_k=1`. The default reduces with atomic adds.
- Cost: about 13 minutes per step, plus about 4 minutes per AIME validation.

New environment variables (all default to the validated behavior):

- `VERL_STEP5_FP8_ACT_QUANT` (default 1): FP8 activation rounding on routed experts.
- `VERL_STEP5_LORA_PER_EXPERT` (default 0): per-expert instead of shared expert factors.
- `VERL_STEP5_ROUTING_AGREEMENT` (diagnostic): logs trainer-router agreement with the replayed routing.
- `VERL_LORA_STAGE_PIN` (default 1): pin the LoRA staging blocks in the vLLM worker.
- `VERL_LORA_DROP_HOST_COPY` (opt-in): release the adapter's host copy in the vLLM worker.

### Design & Code Changes

**Step5 text model** (`verl/models/transformers/step5/`)

- `modeling_step5.py`: the model.
- `loading.py`: FP8 checkpoint loading into FSDP2 shards, and the engine hooks.
- `lora.py`: LoRA attach and adapter export.
- `register.py`: Auto registration.

What it does:

- **Model.** A plain-PyTorch port of the vLLM Step5 text model. It keeps the
  pieces that change numerics:
  - GQA with sliding and sparse (DSA) attention and a head-wise gate;
  - zero-centered RMSNorm and FP32 residual;
  - a FP32 sigmoid router with correction bias;
  - packed routed experts plus a shared expert.

  It has no inference kernels, KV cache or TP. The config class comes from the
  installed vLLM, because transformers has no `step5` type. Registration goes
  through `VERL_USE_EXTERNAL_MODULES=verl.models.transformers.step5.register`.
- **FP8 checkpoint.** Block-FP8 weights are dequantized to BF16 straight into
  each rank's FSDP2 local shard. No rank ever materializes the full model.
- **FP8 activation rule.** Routed experts stored in FP8 see the same 1x128
  UE8M0/E4M3 activation rounding as the serving kernel, with a
  straight-through gradient.
- **LoRA targets.** Attention projections and every MLP, including the routed
  experts through PEFT `target_parameters`. Expert adapters are applied
  unfolded, `s * (x A^T) B^T`, as vLLM does, with FP32 masters. They are never
  folded into a BF16 expert stack. The rank must be a multiple of 8 (grouped
  GEMM alignment).
- **Shared factors.** By default the expert gate/up `A` and down `B` are shared
  across the experts of a layer. The export expands them to the per-expert vLLM
  format.
- **R3.** Recorded rollout routing replaces the native top-k for recorded
  tokens. The weights still come from the trainer router.
- **Packed inputs.** verl's remove-padding rows (`input_ids` + `position_ids`)
  are unpacked into a padded batch and packed back. Any other row whose valid
  tokens do not have strictly increasing positions raises, instead of silently
  attending across sequences. Multi-axis (mRoPE-style) positions are refused.
- **Sync.** The rollout loads the base weights itself. Adapters are streamed
  to it in the per-expert format, using grouped all-gathers. There is no full
  host copy per rank.
- **Engine hooks.** `FSDPEngine` dispatches on `model_type == "step5"` for the
  meta-model build, LoRA attach, sharding/loading, adapter export and the
  refusals below. Other models take the existing path unchanged.

**Known gaps**

- Text-only. The vision tower and MTP layers are not loaded.
- Startup refuses configurations that were not validated or cannot work:
  sequence parallel, liger and fused kernels; activation/param/optimizer
  offload, QAT, a separate reference engine; resuming from
  `lora_adapter_path` (resuming through the verl checkpoint manager works);
  `lora.merge` and merged `hf_model` export (PEFT cannot merge the shared
  expert factors); a LoRA rank not divisible by 8; a base-weight sync
  (`rollout.load_format=dummy` or a non-naive checkpoint engine); adapter
  export from a model built from selected source layers.
- Numerics not yet compared operation by operation with the serving kernels:
  the dense and shared-expert SwiGLU rounds SiLU to BF16 before the
  multiplication, and each routed expert's output is rounded to BF16 before
  the routing weight is applied. Both can move a BF16 result by one ulp. They
  stay as validated until checked against the serving implementation.
- Commit 1 covers tokenizers loaded through `hf_tokenizer`/`hf_processor`. Text
  sent to the rollout server as text is tokenized by the server. Versioned
  tokenizer files (`fast_tokenizer_files`) are not looked up.
- Commit 2 assumes an untagged build is the newest vLLM. An untagged checkout
  of an older vLLM passes the minimum-version checks and fails later inside
  vLLM (for R3 on a pre-0.22 checkout with several KV-cache groups, an
  IndexError in the routed-experts capture). The warning says so; build from a
  tagged checkout to keep the checks.
- Commit 4 checks the R3 prerequisites at startup on the FSDP engine only.
- The grouped adapter gathers are bounded by `max_gathered_bytes`, which is not
  a ceiling on peak memory: a single larger tensor is gathered alone.
- A failure inside a weight sync can still leave the other side waiting, as
  before this PR.

**Rollback / impact on other models**

- Commit 5 is gated on `model_type == "step5"`.
- Commit 4 is gated on `router_replay.mode`, which is off by default, with
  one exception: reference log-probs computed through the actor with the
  adapter disabled (the LoRA reference) now route natively instead of
  replaying the actor's rollout routing, as a separate reference worker does.
  The flag is shared by all engines, so Megatron and VeOmni runs that combine
  a LoRA reference with routing replay change too.
- Commit 1 does nothing unless a probe decodes back with some of its
  whitespace deleted and nothing else changed. A healthy tokenizer costs one
  encode and decode; a tokenizer whose own file also loses the whitespace is
  left alone without a second load.
- Commit 2 changes branch selection only for untagged `0.1.devN` builds
  (prereleases and post-releases of it are parsed as before). A real nightly
  below 0.22, such as `0.21.2.devN`, is still refused for R3. The gates where
  the older path is the safe one (the `mm_processor_cache_gb=0` workaround,
  the NPU 0.23 patch window) keep the raw version. The TCP-store path in
  `stateless_init_process_group` now follows `StatelessProcessGroup`'s fields
  rather than the version, which picks the same path for every tagged release.
- Commit 3 copies LoRA buckets in the vLLM worker as one host block per bucket
  (expert factors in their own block) instead of one clone per tensor, and
  refuses a tensor name sent twice in an adapter-only update. Dropping the
  host copy is opt-in and is ignored with a warning unless the adapter has a
  single slot.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting).
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows): tests exist out of tree (see Test); the e2e path needs a Step5-capable vLLM.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+#
+# GRPO (DAPO-Math-17K, AIME-2024 eval) | Step-5-Preview FP8 | FSDP2 + LoRA | vLLM rollout | 4 nodes x 4 GPUs
+#
+# The trainer runs the verl-native Step5 text model (verl/models/transformers/step5): BF16 projections
+# dequantized from the FP8 checkpoint, FP32 router and norms, FP8 activation rule on the routed experts as in
+# vLLM. Only LoRA adapters are trained and synced (adapter-only sync, LoRA-only checkpoints). The rollout
+# records the routed experts and the trainer replays them (R3).
+#
+# Needs a vLLM with Step5 LoRA serving support, a Ray cluster with nnodes x 4 GPUs, the model on every node,
+# and DAPO-Math-17K / AIME-2024 parquet files with data_source math_dapo / aime_2024. ckpt_dir must be on a
+# filesystem that every node reads (the generated text config is written there and read by every worker).
+#
+# Data order: the reference run shuffled DAPO-Math-17K once with seed 42, kept the first total_steps x 32
+# prompts and read them in order (data.shuffle=false, rollout seed 20261010). This script shuffles the full
+# file with verl's defaults instead; pass data.shuffle=false with a prepared file to follow the run exactly.
+
+set -xeuo pipefail
+
+# ---- user-adjustable ----
+model_path=${model_path:-$HOME/models/Step-5-Preview}
+train_file=${train_file:-$HOME/data/dapo-math-17k.parquet}
+val_file=${val_file:-$HOME/data/aime-2024.parquet}
+ckpt_dir=${ckpt_dir:-$HOME/ckpt/step5_dapo_lora}
+nnodes=${nnodes:-4}
+gpus_per_node=${gpus_per_node:-4}
+rollout_tp=${rollout_tp:-8}
+total_steps=${total_steps:-200}
+
+# Environment for every process. Exporting it here only reaches this shell; Ray workers of an already running
+# cluster inherit their raylet's environment, so the same values are also passed in the job's runtime_env below.
+step5_env=(
+    # The Step5 training model is registered through the external-module hook in every process.
+    VERL_USE_EXTERNAL_MODULES=verl.models.transformers.step5.register
+    # The trainer follows the FP8 activation rule of the served routed experts (default on).
+    VERL_STEP5_FP8_ACT_QUANT=1
+    # Free the adapter's pinned host copy in every vLLM worker once it is active on the GPU.
+    VERL_LORA_DROP_HOST_COPY=1
+    # The reference run used vLLM's V2 model runner; set it explicitly rather than rely on vLLM's default choice.
+    VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
+)
+# Optional switches, forwarded when set: VERL_STEP5_LORA_PER_EXPERT=1 keeps every expert factor per expert,
+# VERL_STEP5_ROUTING_AGREEMENT=1 logs how often the trainer router agrees with the replayed routing.
+for name in VERL_STEP5_LORA_PER_EXPERT VERL_STEP5_ROUTING_AGREEMENT; do
+    if [[ -n ${!name:-} ]]; then
+        step5_env+=("$name=${!name}")
+    fi
+done
+runtime_env_args=()
+for kv in "${step5_env[@]}"; do
+    export "$kv"
+    # Quoted, so Hydra keeps "1" a string: Ray accepts only string env_vars.
+    runtime_env_args+=("++ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.env_vars.${kv%%=*}=\"${kv#*=}\"")
+done
+
+# The checkpoint config nests the text model under text_config; the trainer builds the text model from it.

+import sys
+
+from verl.models.transformers.step5.modeling_step5 import register_step5_training, training_text_config

+    algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=false \

+"""Step5 FP8 checkpoint loading into FSDP2 shards, and the FSDP engine hooks for Step5."""

+import copy

+
+def owned_text_names(mapping, layers):
+    selected = set(range(layers)) if isinstance(layers, int) else set(layers)
+    owned = set()
+    for name in mapping:
+        layer = re.match(r"^model\.layers\.(\d+)\.", name)
+        if (layer and int(layer[1]) in selected) or name.startswith(("model.embed_tokens.", "model.norm.", "lm_head.")):
+            owned.add(name)
+    return owned
+
+
+def source_parameter_name(name, config):
+    name = name.removeprefix("base_model.model.").replace(".base_layer.", ".")
+    ids = getattr(config, "_day0_source_layer_ids", None)
+    if ids is not None:
+        name = re.sub(r"^model\.layers\.(\d+)\.", lambda match: f"model.layers.{ids[int(match[1])]}.", name)
+    return name

+def mark_fp8_experts(model, name):
+    """Routed experts stored in FP8 run with FP8 activations in serving; the trainer forward follows."""
+    if os.environ.get("VERL_STEP5_FP8_ACT_QUANT", "1") == "0":

+    logits = F.pad(z.float(), (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, padding), value=float("-inf")).reshape(regions, 8, groups, dim)
+    mean = (logits.softmax(dim=1) * key).sum(dim=1)
+    # Inference stores BF16-rounded CSA means as unscaled E4M3.
+    return mean.bfloat16().to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()

+def dsa_region_mask(query, key, z, weights, topk):
+    """Unpadded Q [T,G,H,D], shared K/Z [T,1,D], W [T,G,H] → [G,T,T].
+
+    Query must already be E4M3-rounded, as in indexer_norm_rope. The caller
+    must compact each sample's valid tokens independently before this function;
+    physical padding indices are not logical eight-token region indices.
+    """
+    tokens, groups, heads, dim = query.shape
+    if topk < 1 or key.shape != (tokens, 1, dim) or weights.shape != (tokens, groups, heads):
+        raise ValueError("invalid DSA inputs")
+    summaries = csa_region_summaries(key, z).expand(-1, groups, -1)
+    regions = summaries.shape[0]
+    position = torch.arange(tokens, device=query.device)
+    current = position // 8
+    region = torch.arange(regions, device=query.device)
+    historical = region[None, :] < current[:, None]
+    if regions <= topk:
+        selected = historical[None].expand(groups, -1, -1)
+    else:
+        dots = torch.einsum("tghd,rgd->gthr", query.float(), summaries)
+        scores = (dots.relu() * weights.permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(-1).float() / math.sqrt(heads)).sum(dim=2)
+        scores = scores.masked_fill(~historical[None], float("-inf"))
+        # Native selector resolves equal-score boundaries by region index.
+        indices = scores.argsort(dim=-1, descending=True, stable=True)[..., :topk]
+        selected = torch.zeros_like(scores, dtype=torch.bool).scatter(-1, indices, True)
+        selected = selected & historical[None]
+    selected = selected | (region[None, None, :] == current[None, :, None])
+    token_mask = selected.index_select(-1, current)
+    return token_mask & (position[None, None, :] <= position[None, :, None])

+def sparse_gqa(q, k, v, index_q, index_k, index_z, index_weights, *, topk, valid=None, gate=None):
+    """Differentiable main attention, discrete CSA selector, independent samples."""
+    batch, tokens, heads, dim = q.shape
+    groups = k.shape[2]
+    if heads % groups or k.shape != v.shape or k.shape != (batch, tokens, groups, dim):
+        raise ValueError("incompatible sparse GQA shapes")

+        valid = torch.ones((batch, tokens), dtype=torch.bool, device=q.device)
+    outputs = []
+    for sample in range(batch):
+        ids = valid[sample].bool().nonzero().flatten()
+        if ids.numel() == 0:
+            outputs.append(torch.zeros_like(q[sample]))
+            continue
+        mask = dsa_region_mask(
+            index_q[sample, ids], index_k[sample, ids], index_z[sample, ids], index_weights[sample, ids], topk
+        )
+        query = q[sample, ids].reshape(-1, groups, heads // groups, dim).permute(1, 2, 0, 3)
+        key = k[sample, ids].permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(1)
+        value = v[sample, ids].permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(1)
+        attended = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+            query, key, value, attn_mask=mask[:, None], dropout_p=0.0, enable_gqa=True
+        )
+        attended = attended.permute(2, 0, 1, 3).reshape(-1, heads, dim)
+        if gate is not None:
+            attended = (attended.float() * gate[sample, ids].float().sigmoid().unsqueeze(-1)).to(q.dtype)
+        outputs.append(torch.zeros_like(q[sample]).index_copy(0, ids, attended))
+    return torch.stack(outputs)

+def _per_layer(values, layer, default=None):

+class Step5Attention(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config, layer):

+            raise NotImplementedError("Step5 training reference requires bias-free GQA")
+        kind = _per_layer(
+            getattr(config, "_day0_source_layer_types", config.layer_types),
+            layer,
+            "sliding_attention" if layer % 2 == 0 else "full_attention",
+        )
+        self.window = getattr(config, "sliding_window", None) if kind == "sliding_attention" else None
+        other = config.attention_other_setting or {}
+        selected = other if other.get("attention_type") == kind else {}
+        self.heads = selected.get("num_attention_heads", config.num_attention_heads)
+        self.groups = selected.get("num_attention_groups", config.num_attention_groups)
+        self.head_dim = selected.get("head_dim", config.head_dim or config.hidden_size // self.heads)
+        if self.heads % self.groups:
+            raise ValueError("GQA heads must divide into KV groups")
+        dtype, hidden = _dtype(config), config.hidden_size
+        self.q_proj = nn.Linear(hidden, self.heads * self.head_dim, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+        self.k_proj = nn.Linear(hidden, self.groups * self.head_dim, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+        self.v_proj = nn.Linear(hidden, self.groups * self.head_dim, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+        self.o_proj = nn.Linear(self.heads * self.head_dim, hidden, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+        self.q_norm = Step5RMSNorm(self.head_dim, config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.k_norm = Step5RMSNorm(self.head_dim, config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.g_proj = nn.Linear(hidden, self.heads, bias=False, dtype=dtype) if config.use_head_wise_attn_gate else None
+        self.rotary_dim = int(self.head_dim * _per_layer(config.partial_rotary_factors, layer, 1.0))
+        self.theta = _per_layer(config.rope_theta, layer) if isinstance(config.rope_theta, list) else config.rope_theta
+        self.scaling = config.rope_scaling if not config.yarn_only_types or kind in config.yarn_only_types else None
+        self.use_rope = _per_layer(config.use_rope_layers, layer, True)
+        sparse = getattr(config, "sparse_config", None)
+        self.sparse = sparse if sparse and sparse.get("enabled", True) and kind == "full_attention" else None
+        if self.sparse:
+            proxy = sparse.get("proxy_dim", 256)
+            self.index_heads = sparse.get("sparse_indexer_num_heads", 16)
+            providers = sparse.get("num_provider_groups", sparse.get("index_tp_size", 4))
+            if providers != self.groups or self.index_heads % providers:
+                raise ValueError("Indexer provider groups must match main KV groups")
+            self.proxy_dim = proxy
+            self.index_rotary_dim = sparse.get("sparse_indexer_rope_dim", 32)
+            self.topk = sparse.get("topk", 512)
+            self.sparse_indexer_q = nn.Linear(hidden, self.index_heads * proxy, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+            self.sparse_indexer_k = nn.Linear(hidden, proxy, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+            self.sparse_indexer_z = nn.Linear(hidden, proxy, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+            self.sparse_indexer_w = nn.Linear(hidden, self.index_heads, bias=False, dtype=dtype)
+            self.sparse_indexer_q_norm = Step5RMSNorm(proxy, config.rms_norm_eps)
+            self.sparse_indexer_k_norm = Step5IndexerLayerNorm(proxy, config.rms_norm_eps)
+            self.ssmax_s = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(self.heads), requires_grad=False)
+
+    def forward(self, x, positions, valid):
+        batch, tokens, _ = x.shape
+        q = self.q_norm(self.q_proj(x).reshape(batch, tokens, self.heads, self.head_dim))
+        k = self.k_norm(self.k_proj(x).reshape(batch, tokens, self.groups, self.head_dim))
+        v = self.v_proj(x).reshape(batch, tokens, self.groups, self.head_dim)
+        if self.use_rope:
+            q = neox_rope(q, positions, self.rotary_dim, self.theta, self.scaling)
+            k = neox_rope(k, positions, self.rotary_dim, self.theta, self.scaling)
+        gate = self.g_proj(x) if self.g_proj is not None else None
+        if self.sparse:
+            iq = self.sparse_indexer_q_norm(
+                self.sparse_indexer_q(x).reshape(batch, tokens, self.index_heads, self.proxy_dim)
+            )
+            ik = self.sparse_indexer_k_norm(self.sparse_indexer_k(x)).reshape(batch, tokens, 1, self.proxy_dim)
+            iq = neox_rope(iq, positions, self.index_rotary_dim, self.theta, self.scaling)
+            ik = neox_rope(ik, positions, self.index_rotary_dim, self.theta, self.scaling)
+            iq = (
+                iq.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+                .float()
+                .reshape(batch, tokens, self.groups, self.index_heads // self.groups, self.proxy_dim)
+            )
+            iz = self.sparse_indexer_z(x).reshape(batch, tokens, 1, self.proxy_dim)
+            iw = self.sparse_indexer_w(x).reshape(batch, tokens, self.groups, self.index_heads // self.groups)
+            out = sparse_gqa(q, k, v, iq, ik, iz, iw, topk=self.topk, valid=valid, gate=gate)
+        else:
+            out = causal_gqa(q, k, v, valid=valid, window=self.window, gate=gate)

+class Step5DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config, layer):
+        super().__init__()
+        if not config.zero_centered:
+            raise NotImplementedError("Step5 requires zero-centered RMSNorm")
+        self.fp32_residual = config.fp32_residual_connection
+        self.dtype = _dtype(config)
+        self.input_layernorm = Step5RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = Step5RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.self_attn = Step5Attention(config, layer)
+        if layer in _moe_layers(config):
+            if not config.need_fp32_gate or not config.use_moe_router_bias or config.moe_router_activation != "sigmoid":
+                raise NotImplementedError("Step5 requires FP32 sigmoid routing with correction bias")
+            self.moe = Step5MoE(
+                config.hidden_size,
+                config.moe_intermediate_size,
+                config.share_expert_dim,
+                config.moe_num_experts,
+                config.moe_top_k,
+                renormalize=config.norm_expert_weight,
+                routed_scale=config.moe_router_scaling_factor,
+                expert_limit=_per_layer(config.swiglu_limits, layer),
+                shared_limit=_per_layer(config.swiglu_limits_shared, layer),
+                dtype=self.dtype,
+            )
+            # Checkpoint ownership is layers.N.share_expert, not layers.N.moe.share_expert.
+            self.share_expert = self.moe.share_expert
+            del self.moe.share_expert
+        else:
+            self.mlp = Step5MLP(
+                config.hidden_size, config.intermediate_size, _per_layer(config.swiglu_limits_shared, layer), self.dtype
+            )
+
+    def _add(self, x, y):
+        return x.float() + y.float() if self.fp32_residual else x + y
+
+    def forward(self, x, positions, valid, replay=None):
+        x = self._add(x, self.self_attn(self.input_layernorm(x, out_dtype=self.dtype), positions, valid))
+        normalized = self.post_attention_layernorm(x, out_dtype=self.dtype)
+        if hasattr(self, "moe"):
+            shared = self.share_expert(normalized)
+            routed = self.moe(normalized, routed_only=True, replay=replay)
+            output = self._add(shared, routed)
+        else:
+            output = self.mlp(normalized)
+        return self._add(x, output)

+class Step5TextModel(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = config
+        self.embed_tokens = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.hidden_size, dtype=_dtype(config))
+        source_ids = getattr(config, "_day0_source_layer_ids", list(range(config.num_hidden_layers)))
+        if (
+            len(source_ids) != config.num_hidden_layers

+            or any(i < 0 for i in source_ids)

+            x = x.float()

+            # The rollout reports [..., layer, top_k] with one row per layer of the source model, indexed by
+            # layer id; layers without routed experts stay zero.
+            # Source layers this model does not build may carry records; a built dense layer may not.
+            moe_ids = [i for i, layer in zip(self.source_ids, self.layers, strict=True) if hasattr(layer, "moe")]

+                    f"got {tuple(routed_experts.shape)}"
+                )
+            else:
+                dense_ids = [
+                    i
+                    for i, layer in zip(self.source_ids, self.layers, strict=True)
+                    if not hasattr(layer, "moe") and i < routed_experts.shape[-2]
+                ]
+                if dense_ids and bool(routed_experts[..., dense_ids, :].any()):

+                "R3 routing: recorded=%d set_differs=%d experts_not_native=%d top_k=%d",

+    previous = F.pad(seen[..., :-1], (1, 0), value=-1)

+        attention_mask=None,

+        return_dict=None,
+        routed_experts=None,

+            raise NotImplementedError("Training reference uses full sequences without KV cache")

+                f"position_ids must be [batch, tokens] {tuple(shape)}, got {tuple(position_ids.shape)}"

+            and position_ids is not None

+            # sequence. Run them as the padded batch the model was validated on and pack the result back.

+            start = position_ids[0] == 0
+            if bool(((position_ids[0, 1:] <= position_ids[0, :-1]) & ~start[1:]).any()):

+                    "packed position_ids must increase strictly within each sequence (a new sequence starts at 0)"
+                )

+                unpack(input_ids),

+            )

+            return (loss, logits) if loss is not None else (logits,)
+        return CausalLMOutputWithPast(loss=loss, logits=logits)
